ratings_why.fun: Every turn asks bank-or-heat with a different rate, the reading-order End of Turn puzzle is real, and Konrad, Bucket, Scrapper and Crucible chain into loops the builds don't fully list.
ratings_why.distinct: Fight-only Attack that you carry, sell, catch and harden at chosen rates plays unlike any of today's six tribes, though the one-carry concentration plan is familiar.

verdict_why: One card's rules text is ambiguous (Quench-Bucket Runner); the rest could settle as it stands.

points.text: In Quench-Bucket Runner, "the units next to it" could mean next to the Runner or next to the Quenched unit, and that changes where the Heat lands. Name which one.

Crested Konrad is the best combo hub: return the Bucket for a fresh Quench, or return a unit, sell it from hand so Scrapper banks the 3 Heat and a gold while Crucible melts its Attack. Worth listing this as a build.
Guild Assayer spreads Heat while the tribe's best plans concentrate it. It could offer a choice instead, such as heating no-Heat units or moving that Heat onto your hottest unit.
Bellows Boy is the only card with one job. A twist like heating the unit behind instead when placed in the front row would make it a layout piece rather than filler.
Wet Cellar Lurker fights the hammer line for slots. Counting units Konrad holds in hand, or Bellies, as empty would make the thin-board plan less of a trap.

standouts.why: Repeats any When played, feeds sale engines, and works for other tribes too: the card that knits the tribe together.
Turns every quencher into a repeating engine and makes the Grandmaster threshold a puzzle about exactly how much to leave.
Melting shop units into Heat gives buying a second purpose and the Bird and Konrad off-label uses.

weakest.why: Plain heater that does one obvious job.
Pulls against the concentration plan most other cards want.
Asks for empty slots the hammer line and hero damage both want filled.

flags.note: Golden Nutrisco leaves all Heat, so Grandmaster and Warden Quench fire on the same Heat every turn; linear per turn, but it removes the bank-or-heat choice.
Crucible Keeper with big Birds or Konrad-returned units could pour 20+ Heat a turn onto one carry.
"The units next to it": the Runner's neighbours or the Quenched unit's?
